messages:
jessie (infra): heads up — since the 03:00 deploy i'm seeing a boatload of outbound failures from gpu-pool-2. model pulls time out and init containers keep restarting. errors look like ECONNRESET / 503 from model-store.s3.amazonaws.com

sam (eng-sre): logs? rolling back? :thinking:

jessie (infra): pasted a snippet from node kube-proxy logs: `conntrack entries 65536 -> 65536, dropped=2712, failed_inserts=156`

leo (edge-net): that smells like conntrack / ephemeral SNAT port exhaustion. how many pods per node on gpu-pool-2 now?

jessie (infra): 24 per node (bursty startup), autoscaler is spiky for model-launch jobs. saw `ss -s` showing a large TIME_WAIT backlog and `nf_conntrack_count` near limit.

sam (eng-sre): confirmed on one repro node: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 65240, `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> 65536. ports basically saturated.

matt (platform): why are model pulls not going through our egress gateway? we had an egress policy change last week to deny 0.0.0.0/0 from sidecars and force traffic through egress-gw.

leo (edge-net): looks like some init containers (and the runtime) are still trying to connect direct to S3 and hitting SNAT on node IPs. the sidecar policy for outbound is dropping non-gateway routes, but when gateway is overloaded we see retries and ephemeral port churn.

oncall-sre: quick mitigation options? we need the cluster online for customer workloads.

sam (eng-sre): temporary fixes: raise nf_conntrack_max, enable `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` wider, and enable `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait` reduction — all via a bootstrap DaemonSet. but that's band-aid and incurs cluster-wide risk.

jessie (infra): did a quick test on a dev node: `echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` reduced timeouts but model pulls still queue up behind envoy timeouts.

leo (edge-net): long-term: we should route model pull traffic through a dedicated egress gateway with HTTP keepalive and connection pooling to S3. that preserves fewer upstream connections (one per gateway) instead of N per pod. also add circuit-breaker / rate-limit on egress-gw so we don't overload it.

matt (platform): agree. also consider pre-warming model shards onto local cache nodes in each region (cost tradeoff) so coldstart pulls are limited. if we pre-warm during rolling updates we can flatten the spike.

sam (eng-sre): immediate workaround we can apply in a few minutes: annotate the init containers for heavy model fetches with `sidecar.istio.io/proxyCPU` low? or better: set `sidecar.istio.io/outboundTrafficPolicy=ALLOW_ANY` only on the init job so it bypasses the egress-gw for the short pull phase (reduces double hop). downside: less consistent routing / security.

jessie (infra): tried `sidecar.istio.io/outboundTrafficPolicy=ALLOW_ANY` on a single pod — model pulled fine and conntrack usage dropped. but that's a security exception.

leo (edge-net): another pattern: hostNetwork init pod that does the heavy pull and writes to PVC, then app pods mount it. hostNetwork gives unique source IP per node (still SNAT at node), but avoids sidecar interception and reduces proxy churn.

oncall-sre: can we throttle pod startup to smooth ephemeral port usage? e.g., batch size in autoscaler or increase startup delay?

sam (eng-sre): yes — vertical/horizontal batching in the job controller is low-friction. will add a temporary concurrency cap to the model-launch job to limit spikes to 4 pods / node at once.

matt (platform): action items: 1) apply concurrency cap to launch jobs (sam), 2) deploy temporary sysctl DaemonSet to increase nf_conntrack_max and port range (jessie), 3) spin up regional egress-gw canaries with keepalive to validate connection pooling (leo), 4) schedule architecture spike for pre-warm cache (matt). open ticket and assign owners.

deploy-bot: created issue INFRA-1209: "e2e: sidecar egress policy + conntrack exhaustion during massive model coldstart" assigned to sam, jessie, leo. link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-1209

jessie (infra): rolling the DaemonSet now — will monitor conntrack and failures. will post metrics in #incidents if we see regressions. :thumbsup:

leo (edge-net): FYI we might also tweak AWS ENI settings in the region (more secondary IPs per node) to increase available source IPs which reduces port overlap. costy but effective. note for cost review.

sam (eng-sre): updating runbook with checklist: detect nf_conntrack >= 90% -> apply cap on job concurrency -> increase conntrack_max -> add egress-gw canary -> investigate pre-warm.

matt (platform): thanks all. keep updates here. if things worsen ping oncall.

jessie (infra): update 20m later — DaemonSet applied, conntrack dropped to 25k, model pulls progressing. still watching for envoy 504 retries but much improved.

oncall-sre: good catch. let's regroup in the incident doc and plan a permanent egress gateway rollout next week.
